title: Vision Augmentation and Robustness knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Random crops and flips” in this lesson?
options: This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Check image dimensions, channel order, value range, and label/target formats; reuse compatible transforms for validation and inference.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
questions.answer_key: Check image dimensions, channel order, value range, and label/target formats; reuse compatible transforms for validation and inference.
questions.explanation: Random crops and flips: Check image dimensions, channel order, value range, and label/target formats; reuse compatible transforms for validation and inference.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Color transformations”, what should a learner verify?
options: confirm image layout, numeric range, normalization, label format, and that validation/inference do not use random training-only augmentation.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
questions.answer_key: confirm image layout, numeric range, normalization, label format, and that validation/inference do not use random training-only augmentation.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: confirm image layout, numeric range, normalization, label format, and that validation/inference do not use random training-only augmentation.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “MixUp and CutMix”?
options: Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Do not normalize or resize inference images differently from the preprocessing used during training.
questions.answer_key: Do not normalize or resize inference images differently from the preprocessing used during training.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not normalize or resize inference images differently from the preprocessing used during training.
